# Two Columns and a Spanning Title

The first paragraph opens the left column. It describes a river that rises in the mountains, runs north through a wide valley, and reaches the sea after crossing three lakes and a long stretch of marsh.

The second paragraph begins near the foot of the left column and is long enough to continue at the top of the right one. It tells how the valley was settled, first by farmers who drained the lower fields, then by a mill town that grew where the river narrows, and finally by a railway that followed the old towpath. A reader that splits this paragraph at the column break has turned one paragraph into two.

The third paragraph closes the right column. It notes that the marsh is now a reserve, and that the lakes freeze in most winters.
